hgb_experiments.candidate_generation: V3 Top5 plus native V3 Top100; unseen items interleaved Repeat/ALS/CBF/popularity until exactly 200

decision.selection: best of four predeclared feature groups

diagnostics.activity_group_definition: train60 aggregate distinct-item groups retained from baseline evaluation; different from strict50 profile availability (15 cold profiles vs 10 train60 cold users)
interpretation_limits: Cumulative group deltas are contextual ablations, not individual feature importance or causal attribution.
Balanced predict_proba outputs are ranking scores, not calibrated probabilities.
Main holdout was reused across stages; confidence interval after selecting among four groups is descriptive, not independent-test evidence.

Recommended-item catalogue coverage decreases from 228 to 121 items. Popularity Top5 share rises for A/B/C, but selected D is slightly below V3 (56.984% vs 57.238%); do not describe D gain as a higher global-Top5 share.
Candidate-generation recall/oracle metrics use the full GT denominator; measured Top5 gains apply only to the fixed evaluation cohort.
Only 3 of 6225 warm D slots lie outside native V3 Top100, all irrelevant; observed gain is primarily candidate reranking within native PPR/V3 coverage, not successful outside-Top100 expansion.
diagnostics.scope: saved offline predictions and feature snapshots only; no training/refit/inference/raw CSV scan

feature_semantics_limitations: Main holdout repeatedly used before this experiment; bootstrap is descriptive after four-group selection.
Single meta-training target horizon 35 days differs from main70 and test84; balanced outputs are ranking scores, not calibrated probabilities.
Cold users keep the common popularity fallback; negative labels mean no observed strict positive, not dislike.

training_scheme.negatives: all unobserved candidate pairs, not explicit dislikes

kaggle_user_reported.note: scores were reported by the user after manual submissions; this fact extraction did not query Kaggle or verify a screenshot

v1.source: user-reported after first submission; never used for tuning

v3.source: user-reported, never used for parameter selection

v4.source: user-reported after manual V4 submission; no screenshot supplied; not independently checked via Kaggle

limitations: The two example users were selected previously using train activity, not selected now for favourable model results.
Popularity beats PPR and V3 for the chosen heavy user; all personalised methods fall back for the chosen light user.
A watched-overlap proxy is not evidence of enjoyment; programme IDs may combine episode-specific titles.
Participant-reported >80% rule is not independently verified evaluator source code.
Holdout and early-window results were reused for selection; bootstrap intervals are descriptive and not adjusted for that selection.
Earlier-window data occur in main training; early evaluation is temporal robustness rather than untouched confirmation.
Future schedules supply only availability/channel/time for modelling; displayed validation titles/categories are descriptive annotations.
Cold-start counts depend on the interaction definition: the old 60-second activity cohorts are frozen and differ from strict-50 model cold-start.
The selected HGB improves aggregate offline MAP but does not improve AP for either fixed example user; Popularity still beats HGB for the heavy example.
HGB cumulative feature-group differences are contextual ablations, not individual feature importances or causal effects.
Class-balanced HGB predict_proba values are ranking scores and are not calibrated probabilities.
HGB meta-training uses one 35-day historical target window, whereas main validation is 70 days and test is 84 days.
Selected HGB D narrows the offline Top5 catalogue from 228 to 121 programmes. Its popular-Top5 share is slightly lower than V3, 56.984% versus 57.238%.
Reported Kaggle scores come from user statements after manual submissions. Screenshots and direct Kaggle/API verification were not supplied for this report update.

HGB.score_semantics: Balanced predict_proba is an uncalibrated ranking score, not an estimated watch probability.

protocol.ap_definition: sum of precision@rank for first occurrences of relevant items in Top5, divided by min(5, full relevant-set size)

ground_truth.airing_deduplication: one qualifying user/channel/airing irrespective of qualifying source-row count
ground_truth.channel_ambiguity: remove simultaneous different-channel time; each remaining continuous piece is independent
ground_truth.denominator: full canonical airing duration; period clipping never shortens denominator
ground_truth.schedule_policy: existing half-open channel/time index, zero IDs and conflicting airings excluded
ground_truth.sitting: one original log row after exact deduplication; no merging across original rows
ground_truth.source_status: participant description, not confirmed Kaggle judge code; devices and actual switches unobservable

protocol.hgb_evaluation: HGB also uses the same strict >80% validation GT, frozen 1260-user cohort and 6384-item candidate pool; meta-training labels are from the earlier nonoverlapping 35-day target window.
protocol.popularity_training_exception: frozen reference and shared fallback use old >=60 unique seconds train interactions; all seven methods evaluated on identical strict >80% GT/cohort/candidate pool

provenance.hgb_metadata_source: reuse exact title/category pairs already verified under the existing validation-overlap display-mode policy; no new EPG scan or model feature extraction
provenance.metadata_display_policy: mode of raw (title, category) pairs over validation-overlapping airings from first two schedule files; lexical pair tie-break; display only, never model features
provenance.metric_policy: copied from saved artifacts; example AP recomputed independently with exact fractions
